assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to incretin-based therapies, has changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and is now showing benefit in cardiovascular and renal outcomes. It is a clear case of basic physiology becoming a transformative therapy, with very broad and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2, translational work) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a plausible trio. Knudsen led industrial development of long-acting analogues, which is a distinct, drug-development contribution. Mojsov's share of credit is the part most contested in my recollection.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is confirmed by large independent trials over many years and the mechanism is stable. Recognition is timely given the scale of current impact.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the identification of the active GLP-1 fragment is disputed and I have not verified the details.
Whether industrial analogue development (Knudsen) should be recognized alongside the physiology is unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a previously unknown intracellular signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus. It is conceptually original and fundamental, and it informs diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the IRE1/HAC1 signaling logic in yeast and mammals, so a two-person prize is natural. Others in the field (for example in PERK/ATF6 branches or Ron's work) may have a claim, which is not reflected in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and a stable core mechanism. Recognition would be timely to overdue, with prior Lasker recognition as I recall it.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation (for example ISRIB or IRE1 inhibitors) is still early.
Additional contributors to the PERK and ATF6 branches are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and cell physiology causal, millisecond-precision control of genetically defined cells. It is an enabling technology with enormous lasting impact, and channelrhodopsin identification is a clear, original discovery.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth, Boyden and colleagues established neuronal use. Miesenboeck's earlier work complicates the picture. Six credited names exceed three laureates, and any trio omits someone with a serious claim.
assessment.maturity: Very widely reproduced across species and labs. Clinical translation is emerging, for example in vision restoration, but the research impact is already firmly established.
uncertainties: Credit is unavoidably contested among more than three people.
Whether a technology that is a tool rather than a disease mechanism fits the prize framing is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living drugs. Impact on cancer treatment is substantial and clear.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed the costimulated CAR designs and clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Eshhar's earlier CAR concept is not among the credited names, which weakens attribution.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up, though toxicity, relapse and solid-tumor limits remain. Recognition is timely, perhaps slightly early for the full story.
uncertainties: Early conceptual credit (Eshhar and others) is outside the credited names.
Long-term outcomes and applicability to solid tumors are unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data now show large reductions in cervical cancer. This is a rare case of vaccine science with demonstrated cancer prevention at scale.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs at the NCI and Frazer (with Zhou) the Queensland work on VLP assembly; the Georgetown and Rochester groups also contributed. Credited names support a reasonable trio but the priority dispute is real.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data over more than a decade confirm the benefit; timely and arguably strengthening each year.
uncertainties: Priority among several groups developing L1 VLPs is contested.
The prize for HPV was given to zur Hausen in 2008, which may influence perceptions of overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. It is a clear, original and widely adopted pathway.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. This is a natural two-person split, though Ishikawa's early STING work and the cGAMP structural work add some ambiguity. I limit to two names.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation of the pathway; therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is not yet established. Perhaps slightly early on translation but mature on mechanism.
uncertainties: Therapeutic benefit has not been shown.
Credit for STING discovery between Barber and Ishikawa may be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, which transformed spinal muscular atrophy from a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one. It is a landmark for RNA-targeted therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the target sequence, and Bennett (Ionis) led antisense chemistry and development. The pairing is coherent, though Hua and others contributed to the work.
assessment.maturity: Clinical effect is robust and durable across years of follow-up, and it has enabled a wider field of RNA therapeutics. Timely.
uncertainties: Other contributors to the SMN2 splicing work may merit credit.
Is this a medicine prize or better suited to chemistry or other recognition for oligonucleotide chemistry is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5-based adult stem cell organoids produced long-lived three-dimensional epithelial cultures from single stem cells and became a major platform for disease modeling, drug testing and personalized medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell identification and organoid culture; Sato was the first author of the key culture paper. A two-person allocation is clear, though others in organoid biology (for example Sasai on pluripotent-derived organoids) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used, though clinical translation is still developing. Recognition is plausible but could be considered somewhat early for therapeutic impact.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is still mostly prospective.
Overlap with pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work is not captured.
